name: MIDRC Open Data Commons (cardiac CT subset)

n_scans.T1: ~78 studies (study_description CTA CORONARY 39, CCTA HEART 16, Cardiac^COR_* 8, other coronary CTA 15)
n_scans.T2: ~97 studies (LA/pulmonary-vein models, TAVR, congenital heart CT, cardiac morphology, triple rule-out)
n_scans.all_CT: 25,795 CT studies of 207,129 total imaging studies

est_size_gb: T1+T2 ~50-100 GB (unverified estimate, ~0.3-0.5 GB/study); T3 ~2-3 TB
labels: none for cardiac; some COVID annotations elsewhere
license: MIDRC DUA (non-commercial academic). Cl.10: no derivative works of the data, BUT explicitly allows users to create and keep 'annotations and overlays' (University claims no rights; encourages submitting them back). Cl.6: no redistribution of images. Cl.5: every user in the org must register and sign separately.
steps_to_access: 1) Go to https://data.midrc.org, log in (Google/ORCID/InCommon), accept the non-commercial DUA. 2) Every annotator who handles images must register individually (DUA cl.5). 3) In Explorer filter imaging_study: study_modality=CT and study_description in the cardiac list; export manifest; download with gen3-client. Turnaround: same day to a few days (unverified).
provenance: Multi-site US clinical data contributed via RSNA/ACR; independent of ImageCAS. Some TCIA COVID collections mirrored here (not cardiac).
verified: Read DUA text at midrc.org; queried the public Guppy GraphQL aggregation (anonymous) for CT study_description histogram on 2026-10-12 and counted cardiac descriptions; did not download images (needs login).
notes: Counts come from free-text study descriptions, so they are approximate; some T2 entries may be non-contrast. Small, but the cheapest new real-world multi-vendor US CCTA available. DUA explicitly permits annotations: good for sharing labels (share labels + MIDRC IDs, not images).

name: SCAPIS (Swedish CArdioPulmonary bioImage Study) CCTA

n_scans.T1: ~25,000 participants with CCTA (per SCAPIS publications; AIDA says CT from 30,000 individuals in 24 datasets = 4 CT exam types x 6 sites incl. CCTA)

format: DICOM via AIDA Data Hub (download or on-platform DGX compute)
labels: CAC score, stenosis/plaque variables available as tabular data on application
license: Swedish confidentiality law (OSL 24:8) + GDPR. Must return any newly created variables to SCAPIS. Must invite a co-author from each of the 6 host universities. Public release of derived labels very unlikely to be allowed.
steps_to_access: 1) Find a PhD-level PI at a Swedish university/region (applicant must be affiliated with a Swedish research institution). 2) Get Swedish Ethical Review Authority (Etikprovningsmyndigheten) approval naming SCAPIS data. 3) Western legal/privacy office + Swedish host do a confidentiality/GDPR assessment for a foreign party (pseudonymised data, confidentiality agreement). 4) Apply via scapis.org portal; pay 6,000 SEK + VAT initiation and 45,000 SEK + VAT for image data (+10,000 SEK per extra data type, max 75,000). 5) After approval, download via AIDA Data Hub. Turnaround: realistically 6-12 months.
provenance: Independent Swedish general-population cohort (age 50-64), Siemens Definition Flash scanners.
verified: Read scapis.org requirements, access-fee and data-delivery pages and AIDA news page (2024-09-16: full CT set transferred). CCTA participant count is from publications, not verified here.
notes: Largest population CCTA set reachable in principle. A Canadian lab is not eligible directly, only through a Swedish collaborator, and BankID download needs a Swedish identity. Huge, but the highest effort.

name: Local retrospective CCTA at London Health Sciences Centre / St. Joseph's (Western REB)
n_scans: Unknown; a tertiary centre doing clinical CCTA/TAVI CT typically has thousands of studies over 5-10 years (not verified)
license: Local REB approval and a data-sharing agreement with LHSC/Lawson; derived labels shareable only if de-identified and approved
steps_to_access: 1) Western/Lawson REB application for retrospective chart/imaging review with waiver of consent. 2) Lawson/LHSC privacy and PACS export request (de-identification). 3) Store on Western/Alliance storage. Turnaround 2-4 months (typical, unverified).
provenance: New, independent; same institution as the project lead.
verified: Not verified (recommendation only).
notes: Probably the best ratio of new T1/T2 scans to effort after MIDRC, because the lead's institution controls it. Worth checking with the cardiac imaging group.

name: RSNA-STR Pulmonary Embolism CT (RSPECT)
labels: PE presence/location/type, RV/LV ratio (study and image level)
license: RSNA terms: non-commercial (academic research, education); no attempts to identify subjects; 'You may not share or redistribute a copy of any portion or all of the data in any form'; must cite Colak et al. 2021. Sharing derived coronary labels (without images) is a grey zone, so ask [contact removed].
steps_to_access: Anonymous: curl https://pulmonary-embolism-detection.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/rsna-ped-dataset.zip (S3 us-west-2, 534 GB single zip; use range requests or aws s3 cp --no-sign-request). Accepting the RSNA terms is implied by use; MIRA controlled-access page https://mira.rsna.org/dataset/2 also listed.
provenance: 5 international sites (incl. Canadian: Unity Health Toronto). Independent of ImageCAS.
verified: Read the AWS registry YAML and licence text; listed the S3 bucket anonymously and got HTTP 200 on HEAD of the zip (no data downloaded, since it is T3).
notes: Non-gated CTPA; coronaries partly visible, motion blur. Low value per scan.

name: INSPECT (Stanford AIMI)

n_scans.T3: 20,078 CTPA scans in current release (19,438 patients); paper reports 23,248 studies

labels: PE outcome labels, report impressions, EHR
license: Stanford Dataset Research Use Agreement: personal non-commercial research only, no redistribution, no re-identification; the EHRSHOT/AIMI variant bars 'derivative works' of the dataset, so sharing labels needs written permission from AIMI
steps_to_access: 1) Create a Redivis account (https://stanford.redivis.com/AIMI), 2) request access to INSPECT and click-accept the Stanford research use agreement, 3) wait for AIMI approval (days to weeks, unverified), 4) export via Redivis.
provenance: Stanford Health Care CTPA; RadFusion (1,837 CTPA) and AIMI 'CT Pulmonary Angiography' are likely overlapping earlier Stanford PE sets.
verified: Read AIMI dataset page (counts above). Redivis pages are JavaScript-only, so I could not read the exact DUA there.

name: RadFusion and AIMI 'CT Pulmonary Angiography'
n_scans: RadFusion: 1,794 patients' CTPA; CTPA set: count not stated on page
license: Stanford research use agreement (non-commercial, no redistribution)
steps_to_access: Same Redivis route as INSPECT.
provenance: Likely overlaps with INSPECT (same institution and indication).
verified: Read the AIMI pages.

name: Stanford AIMI COCA (Coronary Calcium)
n_scans: ~787 gated calcium-score CT + ~200 non-gated chest CT (third-party counts)
license: Stanford research use agreement, non-commercial
steps_to_access: Redivis: https://stanford.redivis.com/datasets/1vm9-30b7p5srg
verified: Read the AIMI page: 'gated coronary CT ... calcium segmentations' (calcium-score scans are non-contrast).
notes: Non-contrast, so out of scope. I checked the full AIMI catalogue (sitemap, 23 datasets): no CCTA or contrast cardiac CT. The CT sets are COCA, INSPECT, RadFusion, CTPA and SinoCT (head).

verified: Read the BioLINCC ISCHEMIA page: 'Study Datasets Only'.
